summary: The provided document consists of a single sentence describing a Hospital Patient Portal with specific encryption and access control standards. It lacks all architectural diagrams, functional requirements, data models, API specifications, and compliance mapping details necessary for engineering implementation.

risk_factors.title: Absence of Data Privacy Framework
risk_factors.description: The document mentions HIPAA but provides no details on data classification, retention policies, or GDPR compliance for EU patients, creating a high risk of regulatory non-compliance.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define data classification levels (PHI, PII, Non-PHI), specify retention periods, and implement GDPR-compliant data subject rights workflows (access, erasure, portability).

risk_factors.title: Missing Audit Trail Specification
risk_factors.description: While RBAC is mentioned, there is no specification for immutable audit logging, which is a critical HIPAA requirement for tracking access to PHI.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify an append-only audit log system with cryptographic hashing to ensure immutability, capturing user, action, timestamp, and resource accessed.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Interoperability Standards
risk_factors.description: The document does not specify HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards for data exchange, which are essential for a hospital portal to integrate with EHR and imaging systems.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define FHIR R4 resource models for patient data and DICOM web services for imaging access, including specific API endpoints and data formats.
